# WCAG 2.2 coverage

**Generated by `npm run coverage`.** Do not edit by hand; CI fails if it is
stale. Source of truth: `verify/wcag-2.2.json` (the criteria) and each skill's
`**Criteria:**` line (which skill claims to address what).

## The honest summary

Three different things are counted separately here on purpose. Collapsing them
into a single percentage would give a bigger number and a false one.

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Criteria in WCAG 2.2 | 86 |
| Criteria **addressed by a skill** | **70** (81%) |
| Criteria with an **executable fixture** | **9** |
| Fixture cases | 14 across 10 skills |
| Skills | 33 |

### By conformance level

| Level | In WCAG 2.2 | Addressed | Coverage |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 31 | 31 | 100% |
| AA | 24 | 24 | 100% |
| AAA | 31 | 15 | 48% |

Level A and AA are where conformance claims are made, so those are the columns
that matter. AAA criteria are included because several of them are what
practitioners actually need — SC 1.4.6 Contrast (Enhanced) and SC 2.5.5 Target
Size (Enhanced) especially.

**"Addressed" does not mean "verified".** It means a skill names the criterion
and gives a procedure for it. Only the fixture column is executed.

## Not covered, and why

16 criteria have no skill. That is a deliberate state for the first group and a backlog for the second.

**Correctly absent — no design procedure can satisfy these.** Each is decided somewhere other than the code, so a "skill" would be a list of things to ask a different team for:

- SC 1.2.6 Sign Language (Prerecorded) — sign language interpretation is a media-production task, not a markup one
- SC 1.2.7 Extended Audio Description (Prerecorded) — extended audio description is a media-production task
- SC 1.2.8 Media Alternative (Prerecorded) — media alternative for time-based media is a media-production task
- SC 1.2.9 Audio-only (Live) — live audio-only alternatives are a scheduling and staffing decision
- SC 1.4.7 Low or No Background Audio — low or no background audio is decided in the recording, not the code
- SC 1.4.9 Images of Text (No Exception) — images of text (no exception) is a design-direction constraint
- SC 2.2.3 No Timing — no timing is an architectural decision that cannot be patched in later
- SC 2.2.4 Interruptions — interruptions is a product decision about what may be sent at all
- SC 2.2.5 Re-authenticating — re-authenticating is a session-architecture decision
- SC 2.4.9 Link Purpose (Link Only) — link purpose (link only) conflicts with the in-context guidance the library gives
- SC 3.1.3 Unusual Words — unusual words needs a glossary, which is editorial
- SC 3.1.4 Abbreviations — abbreviations needs an editorial expansion policy
- SC 3.1.5 Reading Level — reading level is a copywriting standard, not a markup change
- SC 3.1.6 Pronunciation — pronunciation needs per-word pronunciation markup and is rarely applicable
- SC 3.3.5 Help — help is a documentation and support-surface question
- SC 3.3.6 Error Prevention (All) — error prevention (all) is a product-flow decision

**Backlog — procedural, and a skill should exist:**

- None right now.

## Fixtures

A fixture is a pair of real HTML documents. `before.html` must trip the axe
rules the fixture names; `after.html` must be **completely clean** — zero axe
violations of any impact, including best-practice rules. That second requirement
is what stops a skill from fixing one thing and quietly breaking another.

| Skill | Fixture cases |
|---|---|
| `accessible-forms` | 2 |
| `accessible-name` | 2 |
| `fix-color-contrast` | 1 |
| `headings-and-landmarks` | 2 |
| `modal-dialog` | 1 |
| `page-title-and-language` | 1 |
| `semantic-html` | 2 |
| `svg-and-icons` | 1 |
| `wcag22-new-criteria` | 1 |
| `zoom-reflow-text-spacing` | 1 |

### What fixtures cannot prove

Automated checks establish a minority of real accessibility problems. axe-core
finds what is mechanically decidable in a rendered DOM: a missing accessible
name, a contrast ratio, a skipped heading level, a viewport that blocks zoom. It
cannot tell you that a custom widget is unusable from a keyboard, that a live
region announces the wrong thing, or that a dialog loses the user's place. Every
fixture here is chosen from the decidable subset, and every skill whose subject
is *not* decidable says so in its own `## Verify` section.

One concrete example of where the boundary sits, and the reason the
[`accessible-forms`](../skills/accessible-forms/) fixture is built the way it
is: axe-core's `label` rule accepts a non-empty `placeholder` as a label. A
placeholder-only field therefore passes a full automated audit and still fails
SC 3.3.2 the moment someone starts typing and the label vanishes. A clean axe
report is not evidence that a form is usable, and this library does not claim it
is.
